passage:
Friday: Yogesh had been counting days since the letter came. The cousins from Pune were coming Saturday. He cleaned the shelf and set out his carrom board and the building-block set.
Saturday: The cousins tumbled in with bags. Dhruv, the youngest, went straight for the blocks. Yogesh bit his lip, then said, "Take the red ones. I will show you how the bridge goes." Everyone got a turn at carrom, even the little ones.
Sunday: Yogesh caught himself saying, "No, you have to stand here!" Dhruv's face fell. Yogesh stopped, said, "Sorry, you pick the next game," and Dhruv grinned.

qa.q: Where were the cousins coming from?
qa.a: The cousins were coming from Pune.

qa.q: What was Yogesh feeling on Friday, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He was excited; he had been counting days since the letter came and cleaned the shelf to get ready.

qa.q: What went wrong on Sunday and how did Yogesh fix it?
qa.a: He started ordering Dhruv around and Dhruv's face fell. Yogesh stopped, said sorry and let Dhruv pick the next game.

qa.q: How might Dhruv have felt when Yogesh told Dhruv where to stand?
qa.a: Dhruv probably felt bossed around and a little hurt, since the fun turned into being told what to do until Yogesh apologised.

grounding: A child excited about visiting cousins shares toys and includes everyone, and corrects himself when he starts ordering people around.

passage: The community hall was full of wedding lights and the smell of halwa, and Siddharth had been bouncing since breakfast. His cousins from Amritsar had arrived! He dragged Gurpreet and three smaller cousins to the corner where he'd hidden his box of cars. 'Okay, rules. I'm the race boss. Gurpreet, you're only allowed the blue truck. You little ones just watch.' Within five minutes the little ones had wandered off, and Gurpreet was sitting on the stage steps, chin in his hands. Siddharth's excitement drained away. This wasn't how he'd imagined it. He picked up the box and walked over. 'Sorry. Everybody picks one car. And you choose the track.' Gurpreet grinned and built a ramp from a chair cushion, and the little ones came running back.

qa.q: Where had Siddharth hidden his box of cars?
qa.a: In the corner of the community hall.

qa.q: What happened to Siddharth's excitement after five minutes, and why?
qa.a: It drained into disappointment, because bossing everyone around made them leave.
Apologising, letting everyone pick a car and letting Gurpreet choose the track.

qa.q: How did Gurpreet feel about being allowed only the blue truck?
qa.a: Bored and left out, so he sat on the stage steps with his chin in his hands.

grounding: A boy excited about visiting cousins spoils the fun by bossing, then shares and includes everyone.

passage:
Friday. Mridul counted the hours until his cousin Sonali's train came in from Jaipur. He'd made a list and stuck it on the fridge: kite flying, the water park, a ghost story night.
Sunday. By the second day, Mridul was bossing. 'No, we're doing the list in order. You can't just play carrom.' Sonali went quiet and sat with Nani, shelling peanuts. Mridul felt a strange hollow in his stomach. He had wanted this for months, so why wasn't it fun?
Tuesday. Mridul tore the list in half. 'Your half,' he said, handing it over. 'You pick.' Sonali picked carrom first. He lost three games in a row and laughed harder than he had all week.

qa.a: Kite flying, the water park and a ghost story night.

qa.q: What was Mridul feeling when the strange hollow came into his stomach?
qa.a: He felt disappointed and uneasy, sensing that his bossing was spoiling the visit he had been so excited about.

qa.q: What did Mridul do on Tuesday that brought the fun back?
qa.a: He tore the list in half and let Sonali choose, sharing the plans instead of ordering her around.

qa.q: What was it like for Sonali on Sunday?
qa.a: She felt pushed around and left out, so she went quiet and sat with Nani.

grounding: Over several days a boy excited for his cousin's visit learns that bossing ruins the fun and sharing brings it back.
